messages:
mila.sales: Quick help pls — CartQuick POC is failing during a bulk embed import, hitting lots of 429s. Demo tomorrow morning, customer blocked. tenant=cartq-1122.

andre.eng: Which endpoint and are they batching client-side or server-side? Any sample error?

mila.sales: /v1/embeddings, client is doing many small batches (50 reqs concurrently) rather than a few big ones. Sample client error: `HTTP 429 Rate limit exceeded (route=embeddings)` and request id 0xfeedbeef.

lee-sre: Pulling logs for request 0xfeedbeef now. One sec.

lee-sre: Log excerpt:
```
[2026-04-02T09:05:12Z] WARN rate_limiter: REJECT tenant=cartq-1122 route=/v1/embeddings reason=BURST_WINDOW token_count_est=4800 req_count=62 window=60s allowed_reqs=60 tokens_remaining=150000 daily_budget=2000000 req_id=0xfeedbeef
```

andre.eng: Looks like they tripped a burst window guard (reqs) while also approaching daily token budget. Two levers: reduce concurrency or bump per-route request cap temporarily. Also if client sends token_hint header we can account by tokens not requests.

mila.sales: Customer says changing client will take hours. Can we do a temp config so they can finish tonight?

billing-bot: NOTICE: tenant=cartq-1122 daily_token_usage=1,860,000 / daily_limit=2,000,000 (93%). Potential overage if we increase tokens. Billing escalation required for temporary token increases.

lee-sre: We can increase per-route req cap from 60 -> 300 for 3 hours. But if they continue with tiny batches they'll hit token budget quickly. Recommend also enabling `coalesce_small_requests=true` for this tenant to fold single-item calls. That reduces reqs by estimated 35%.

andre.eng: I'll apply the coalesce toggle now (safe). Pushing config: `rb config set tenant=cartq-1122 coalesce_small_requests=true` -> applied.

ops-tool: CONFIG EVENT: coalesce_small_requests=true applied for tenant=cartq-1122 by andre.eng at 2026-04-02T09:10:05Z.

mila.sales: Thanks. Billing on the call now — can we get a short-lived per-route bump and a token buffer?

billing-bot: Billing approves a one-time token buffer of +300,000 tokens upon request from sales manager, with charge-back. Approve to proceed? (yes/no)

mila.sales: yes, approve. Charge to internal trial budget.

lee-sre: Applying per-route bump -> per_route_reqs=300 window=60s for route=/v1/embeddings tenant=cartq-1122 until 2026-04-02T12:10:05Z.

ops-tool: POLICY UPDATE: per_route_reqs override applied tenant=cartq-1122 route=/v1/embeddings new_limit=300 expires=2026-04-02T12:10:05Z (operator=lee-sre).

andre.eng: Monitor the metrics — dashboards show request drop rate and token burn. Give me 5-10m.

billing-bot: NOTICE: Temporary token buffer applied. New_day_token_budget=2,300,000 expires=2026-04-02T12:10:05Z.

mila.sales: Customer reports 429s dropped by ~80% after the coalesce change and bump. Demo team unblocked, thank you!

nina-devex: Follow-up: I'll draft a 1-pager for sales with recommended POC patterns: use token_hint header, prefer larger batches, avoid >20 concurrent requests for embeddings, and request dry-run import flow. Will drop in #docs by EOD.

andre.eng: Tech note: command to reproduce logs: `rb logs --tenant cartq-1122 --filter RATE_LIMIT --since 1h | tail -n 50` Also check dashboard: /dash/quotas/cartq-1122.

lee-sre: Postmortem TODOs: 1) add clearer 429 error message that indicates whether limit is per-route vs token-budget, 2) surface token_budget percentage in rate-limit headers, 3) consider auto-coalesce for trial tenants.

mila.sales: Closing — demo successful. Customer asked for best-practice doc and a sample client config. I'll follow up with links. Thanks team :clap:
